219	## 9. Decisions
220	
221	No POSITIONS entry covers these. I acted on the readings given.
222	
223	1. **(ii) is confined to the exclusion test.** It is an added way to be valid, beside `subtypeED` and `emptyED`. This is how the existential-reduction probe confined its own `emptyED` (`perf-probes/existential-reduction/REPORT.md`, decisions, item 2), and how the brief confines (i).
224	   - The alternative is to read the bounds in every reduction. I measured it as the variant `global` (section 3): no further move on this library. It reaches specificity and the Return Type Rule, so it would need its own tests.
225	2. **(ii) reads the bounds in the constraint generator, not in the solver.** A parameter at the top of the body is read as its bounds, in one more conjunct.
226	   - Alternatives: teach `Formula`'s unifier to derive equalities from an upper bound and a non-exclusion constraint, the paper's `unify` over its full constraint language (larger, in a file that every inference uses). Or meet each parameter with its bounds in place (`X & B`), which crashes (section 8).
227	   - Soundness: each instance of `X` lies below `B`, so the conjunct only weakens what the meet's being nonempty already implies.
228	3. **(ii)'s emptiness is decided disjunct by disjunct.** Each disjunct uses only the equalities that the unifier takes from it, which that disjunct implies.
229	   - `reduceED`'s path takes the first unifiable disjunct of an `Or` (`Formula.scala:793-798`), which is not implied by the whole. So I did not reuse it for an emptiness test.
230	   - A disjunct whose unification fails, or whose solution breaks a bound, counts as not empty. This choice can only refuse more.
231	4. **(i) is built from the declaration's own parameters.** It uses `FunctionalMethod.ast`, by the same steps as the plain arrow (the trait's replacer and the own parameters' renaming), only where they differ from `parameters()`, that is, only for a self type read from the F-bound. A self type from a `comprises` clause is left as it is.
232	5. **I ran the full check alone twice** (`full`, `full2`), though the brief takes the earlier report's numbers as the starting values. The site comparison needs a site list, and the earlier one was not on disk. The totals match that report's 191.
233	6. **The probes use the word operator `PLUS`,** as the earlier probe's did, so that they read the same with and without the full check.
234	7. **I ran the compiled tests three times** (no shadow, the full check alone, the full check with both shadows), so that a change could be laid to the full check or to the shadows. None changed.
235	
236	## 10. For FACTS
237	
238	- **The fact.** With the full symbolic-operator check on, the compiled checker refuses the 8 pairs between `AdditiveGroup`'s `+`/`-` and the generic array-and-scalar block only for two gaps of its exclusion test. Reading a self-typed trait's `self` as `C[\X\] & X` in that test, and the static parameters' bounds in its reduction's constraint, clears all 8 and moves no other site of the distance stage (191 to 183) or of the count stage (102 to 98). The self type alone clears none of the 8; the bounds alone clear the four scalar-on-the-left pairs.
239	- **What it means for the work.** P-157's stated reason, that the two cannot both pass "while it reads a self-typed trait's `self` in a signature as the plain trait type", holds of the checker as built. A checker change that keeps the signatures plain for specificity and the Return Type Rule removes it with no library line. That checker change would also need (ii); (i) alone does not suffice.
240	- **The number.** 8: the distance stage's `#class L1` row under the full check.
241	- **The command and its output.** `explorations/perf-probes/self-type-exclusion/run.sh <out> <scratch> selfexc bounds` gives `#total 183`; with no word, `#total 191`.
242	- **The detail.** Sections 3 to 5 of this note.
243	
244	## 11. Commands worked out
245	
246	- `shadow.py <tree> <out-dir> [selfexc] [bounds] [global] [keepvar]`: writes the full-check shadow (with `catch`) and this probe's shadows from the tracked sources. Each edit must match once.
247	- `run.sh <out> <scratch> [words]`: the distance stage with those shadows.
248	- `count.sh <out> <scratch> plain|full [words]`: the count stage with them. Its one changed line of `checker-count/run.sh` puts `$EXTRA_CP` first on the class path.
249	- `tests.sh <scratch> plain|full [words] -- <tests>`: compiled `.test` files in one JVM, with the shadow classes first and a private copy of the caches.
250	- `sites.py <errors.tsv> <errors.tsv> [<run.txt> <run.txt>]`: the site-by-site comparison of two distance runs, renamed variables masked, and of their caught crashes.
251	- `-Dprobe.excdebug=true` on a shadowed checker's JVM prints each meet that (ii) decides, with its constraint.
252	
253	## 12. Questions for the curator (decisions not taken)
254	
255	1. **P-157: withdraw it, or land it.**
256	   - The way that this probe measures is a checker rung that builds (i) and (ii) in the exclusion test: `Vector` and `Matrix` stay `AdditiveGroup`s, and the scalar block stays. It reads anew P-146's sentence "The method signatures keep the plain trait type" for the exclusion test only. It needs the extender rule that P-146 already builds, and it leaves specificity and the Return Type Rule as P-146 has them.
257	   - The alternative, A2 as P-157 decides, gives the same 183 with 6 library lines, and gives up `SUM` and `zero` over vectors.
258	   - Default: withdraw P-157 and brief the checker rung. It clears the same 8, brings nothing on the library, the count stage or the 35 tests, keeps the team's `Vector` and `Matrix`, and touches no library, walk or model line.
259	2. **The form of (ii) in that rung.**
260	   - In the exclusion test only, as measured, or in every existential reduction (`global`).
261	   - Default: the exclusion test only. It is narrower, the library shows no difference, and the global form reaches specificity and the Return Type Rule untested.
262	3. **Row 786's `tint`.**
263	   - It stays refused under (ii). Accepting it needs a further rule: an existential whose parameter's merged bounds exclude each other has no instance, so `Bottom` is not taken as a static argument.
264	   - Default: keep the refusal, as row 786 records P-26 pointing to it, and leave the row `CONTESTED`.
265	4. **The solver's recursion (section 8).**
266	   - File the drafted row now, or only if the rung's form of (ii) meets it.
267	   - Default: file it now. It is the checker's own termination gap, and a rung that reads bounds by meeting a parameter with them in place would meet it.
